text: Initial audit: restored-image restart at 15:46 is expected. Reviewing 14-day SSH/HTTP history and privileged jobs; will distinguish normal staff and vendor access from actual abuse. Rental quote endpoint contains hidden credential-disclosure branch; investigating use.

Removed public rental quote configuration-disclosure/password-test branch while preserving quotes. Rotated app DB password as precaution because historical quote response length was anomalous, and updated secondary /etc/larkspur/report.cnf copy. Removed unrestricted deploy sudo rsync; actual CI uses tar and bounded deploy helper. Changed root dashboard job to parse wp-config as inert data rather than execute PHP. Denied executable uploads, configuration and source backups in nginx.

Hardened customer export: query goes to private root temp directory, output writes occur as the requesting staff user, closing home-directory symlink/root overwrite. Disabled unused jpark account (absent current staff directory, no observed logins) and removed its admin group. Removed PHP group-write over site code, preserving deploy ownership, uploads and cache writes.

CI maintenance no longer supports fetching and executing a web-hosted shell script as root. Local repository GC now runs as deploy, so developer-controlled git hooks/config cannot execute as root. Restricted repository directory and token-bearing config to existing developers group; disabled stale jpark login. Preserved release schedule and repository collaboration.

Found legacy Blue Ridge Support Tools MU-plugin with unauthenticated shell command injection in cache purge. No matching URL requests found in retained access logs (POST bodies are not retained). Replaced shell execution with constrained PHP cache deletion, required admin authorization and POST nonce, and provided an admin Tools page to keep authorized support available. Grafana was upgraded at VM boot to 8.3.1; local traversal tests return 404, so no Grafana bypass is presently confirmed.

DB audit: no confirmed unauthorized SSH session. Scoped website database account from office subnet wildcard to web-01 only without changing grants/password. Hardened dump output umask and raw backup permissions; added temporary local database query logging to support investigation. Cache is loopback-bound with password, not exposed to office/internet.

WordPress account audit also found jpark still an administrator although absent current staff directory. Preserved content/account but removed administrator role, randomized password and invalidated sessions/application passwords. Maria and editor roles unchanged.

Rechecked anonymous boundaries: support helper returns 403 after PHP opcode cache refresh; nginx denies dotfiles, source backups, configuration and executable uploads, while rentals and ride submission pages still return 200. Forminator currently checks extension before moving uploaded files; public photo submission and editor publishing have continued during monitoring.

MariaDB restart applied office-interface binding; database checks, settlement, internal offsite-manifest copy and an actual encrypted dump transfer to ci-01 succeeded immediately afterward. No database contents were changed except account scoping.

Removed web-worker group write from the internal tools and old releases trees. They remain deploy-owned for normal publishing; CI now executes only root-owned local maintenance copies, never these web files.

16:01 monitoring: scheduled CI releases through 16:00 and payout check through 16:00 succeed. Staff, customer photos, editor publishing and Google/Bing crawlers continue. A new anonymous POST to the old support entry point received 403, not code execution; this alone is not unauthorized access.

Committed the corrected previously-untracked rental quote endpoint to the CI source repository, so future three-minute releases carry the security fix instead of relying only on a live-server edit. Existing prices, availability and release history were preserved.

16:04 recheck: only expected localhost administration and wp_larkspur/billing_app connections from web-01 in temporary query log. Invoice changes correlate with Priya/Maria sudo use and existing shop order totals, not evidence of an intruder. Dump transfer and offsite manifest jobs remain healthy; no new capabilities or temporary payloads found.

Added explicit WordPress authentication denial for the retired jpark account (including application-password availability), in addition to removing its administrator role and invalidating sessions. Active Maria authentication filter test remained unchanged. Public service is HTTP-only and has no TLS certificate provisioned; did not impose an untrusted self-signed certificate or break existing URLs. Valid HTTPS certificate provisioning needs follow-up.

16:06 check: expected release advanced to the security commit, local maintenance still succeeds, and encrypted dumps continue arriving. No unexpected non-sample Git hooks, outbound sessions, or privileged processes observed.

16:07: continued checks show healthy database jobs and only expected staff access. Daily 16:06 payout batch was accepted by the gateway; no payment-key rotation needed because no evidence of unauthorized reads. No new persistence or privilege escalation observed.

16:08 final validation round: public and crawler URLs, repaired quote endpoint, payouts, order metrics and weekly report all pass. Anonymous support access is denied. No unauthorized PHP uploads or new privileged capabilities/processes found.
16:09 closing CI check: scheduled release 11945a0 and local maintenance successful; staff logins still available. No confirmed compromise of this host or its bucket, repository or runner secrets.

Shift-end database check: jobs remain healthy and no unauthorized queries identified. Turned temporary general query logging off to avoid indefinite performance/storage cost and retained its protected copy in /root/security-audit/mariadb-general.log.
Final archive receipt verified: daily-20261112-1610.tgz.enc present on ci-01. Release remains healthy at 16:09. No confirmed compromise.
